prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Instant starter pet flow bypass [adoption, new_flow]: predicted +12.0%, measured +10.4% (p=6.9e-05), won
- round 1: Move sign-in after pet selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +10.0%, measured +7.0% (p=4.5e-05), won
- round 1: Clear control instructions on home intro [finish, copy]: predicted +8.0%, measured +5.9% (p=0.110251), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Desktop permission check during setup [home, wait_info]: predicted +4.0%, measured +0.5% (p=0.817329), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Two-column progress view for path selection [choose_path, layout]: predicted +6.0%, measured -0.2% (p=0.880941), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop pet launchpad redesign [finish, redesign]: predicted +3.0%, measured -12.1% (p=0.002132), stopped early: finish worse
- round 2: Generation status notification on wait screen [home, notification]: predicted +4.0%, measured -0.6% (p=0.762734), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Account recovery safety hint on sign-in [sign_in, hint]: predicted +1.0%, measured -3.5% (p=0.025915), lost: worse
- round 2: Simplified path selection guidance [choose_path, copy]: predicted +0.0%, measured +0.7% (p=0.629925), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Bypassing onboarding steps directly (new_flow) significantly improves user conversion.
Reordering friction by moving sign-in after pet selection (reorder) significantly improves conversion.
Copy improvements, permission checks during setup, and layout changes showed no clear effect.
Predictions consistently overestimated actual measured gains across all tests.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Bypassing onboarding steps directly (new_flow) significantly improves conversion.
Reordering friction by moving sign-in after pet selection (reorder) significantly improves conversion.
Major redesigns (redesign) and sign-in hints (hint) significantly hurt performance.
Copy updates, permission checks, layout changes, and notifications showed no clear effect.
Predictions consistently overestimated actual measured gains across tests.
